steps: Shape your dominant hand into an open hand with the fingers together and slightly relaxed.
Place the palm of the hand against the side of your cheek, near the chin.
Stroke downward along your cheek as if pulling at an imaginary beard.
Exaggerate the length of the stroke, because a longer pull means more experience.
Keep your face relaxed and thoughtful, like an elder recalling a long life.
tip: Think of an old man stroking his beard as he reflects on life experience; Lifeprint notes a criss-cross variant means very familiar with.

steps: Hold your dominant hand up in front of you with the thumb and index finger pinched together.
Imagine you are holding a small metal key between the pinched fingertips.
Push the imaginary key forward into an imaginary lock at chest height.
Twist your wrist twice, as if turning the key inside the lock.
Keep the palm facing sideways while twisting; a single twist instead means the verb to lock.
tip: Two twists mean the noun keys; shorten it to one twist and the sign becomes the verb LOCK.

steps: Hold both hands open with the fingers together and the palms facing inward.
Touch your fingertips to the upper part of your torso, near the chest.
Move both hands downward together and touch the lower part of your torso.
Make the two touches distinct, first high and then low, to outline the whole body.
Keep your expression neutral; the sign simply marks the full span of the torso.
tip: Two touches, chest then waist, trace the full body from top to bottom.

steps: Shape both hands into bent B handshapes, with the fingers together and slightly curled.
Hold the hands in front of your chest with the fingertips pointing upward.
Brush the fingertips upward on or just in front of your chest.
Repeat the upward brush once more, for two brushes in total.
Keep the palms facing your chest and the movement short and quick.
tip: The quick upward brushes suggest fresh, rising youth.

steps: Shape both hands into F handshapes, with the thumb and index finger touching.
Turn the F hands sideways so the palms face inward toward your body.
Start with the hands in front of your belly, close together.
Arc both hands up and out to the sides, then bring them together in front of your chest.
End with the F fingertips meeting at chest height in a firm, settled stop.
tip: The big arc rising to the chest shows something held in high value; Lifeprint also glosses it as worthy.

steps: Shape both hands into flat B handshapes, with the fingers together and extended.
Hold the non-dominant hand still in front of you, its palm facing your dominant side.
Face the dominant palm toward the non-dominant hand.
Move only the dominant hand forward, sliding it off the front of the non-dominant hand.
Keep the non-dominant hand frozen while the dominant hand moves away.
tip: This sign also means major, discipline, and career; for an open field of land, use the AREA-based sign instead.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into an E handshape, with the fingers curled and the thumb tucked.
Hold the E hand up at shoulder height with the palm facing forward.
Move the hand in a short straight line toward your right.
Keep the handshape fixed while it travels; east sits to the right on a map.
Use a neutral face, and note the same E hand moves other ways for north, south, and west.
tip: On a map east is to the right, so the E hand simply slides right.

steps: Extend your dominant arm in front of you with the palm facing up.
Hold the index finger up while the other fingers stay folded down.
Make small circular motions, about the size of a coin, with the index finger.
Drive the movement from your shoulder and elbow, keeping the wrist steady.
Keep your expression neutral; the sign also means alone or only depending on context.
tip: One finger drawing small circles pictures one person alone; Lifeprint notes it also covers alone, only, and something or someone.

steps: Extend your dominant arm in front of you with the palm facing up.
Hold the index finger up while the other fingers stay folded down.
Make small circular motions, about the size of a coin, with the index finger.
Drive the movement from your shoulder and elbow, keeping the wrist steady.
Let the surrounding sentence carry the meaning, since the same sign also means single or alone.
tip: Same production as SINGLE; only the context tells listeners you mean something rather than alone.

steps: Shape both hands into flat B handshapes, with the fingers together and extended.
Hold the non-dominant B hand upright in front of your chest, palm facing your dominant side.
Bring the dominant B hand up beneath the non-dominant hand.
Slide the dominant hand under it so the two hands stack into a taller pile.
The added hand shows an extra amount joining the original one.
tip: The dominant hand literally adds to the pile; Lifeprint glosses the same sign as in addition to and extra.

steps: To introduce the word in a new conversation, fingerspell P-A-S-S-W-O-R-D with your dominant hand.
Shape the same hand into an A handshape, a fist with the thumb pressed along the side.
Tap your lips twice with the back of the thumb, keeping the palm facing toward you.
Keep the taps light and quick; once the meaning is clear, the sign alone can mean password.
Mouth a word shape close to password while signing to mark the intended meaning.
tip: PASSWORD is the sign PRIVATE with a password-shaped mouth morpheme; always fingerspell it on first reference in a conversation.
